revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Real Estate
revealWordProblem.text: Terrance is helping his grandmother sell her house. He uses a real estate website to look at the recent sale prices of similarly‑sized houses in their area and collects the prices in the table shown. What would be a fair, but competitive, selling price for Terrance’s grandmother’s house? Use the median to justify your answer.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort the 16 sale prices from least to greatest: $160,000, $199,900, $239,900, $269,900, $307,000, $382,900, $385,400, $401,785, $402,400, $405,400, $423,400, $426,400, $454,400, $457,400, $460,400, $485,250. With 16 values (an even number), the median is the average of the 8th and 9th values: ($401,785 + $402,400) ÷ 2 = $804,185 ÷ 2 = $402,092.50. A fair, competitive selling price would be around $402,000, since that's the middle of the market and isn't pulled up or down by the lowest sale ($160,000) or the highest sale ($485,250).

vocabulary.definition: Measures that describe a data set's center: average, middle value, and most frequent value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Medidas que describen el centro de un conjunto de datos: promedio, valor central y valor más frecuente.

vocabulary.definition: The average. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio. Suma todos los números y divide entre cuántos hay.
vocabulary.visual: Mean of 2, 4, 6: add them (2+4+6=12), divide by 3 → mean = 4
vocabulary.cloze: The average found by adding all values and dividing by how many there are is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 → the middle (3rd) value is 5, so median = 5
vocabulary.cloze: The middle value of a data set when the numbers are in order is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: The number that shows up most often.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que aparece más veces.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7 → 3 appears twice (most often), so mode = 3
vocabulary.cloze: The value that appears most often in a data set is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 10, 12, 11, 13, 50 → 50 is far from the others, so 50 is an outlier
vocabulary.cloze: A value that is much larger or smaller than the rest of the data is an ___.

examples.why: It is far from the other values.
It fits in with the rest of the values.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: If most values cluster in the center with fewer at the ends, the distribution is symmetric
vocabulary.cloze: The way data values are spread out is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: 8, 9, 10, 11 has low variability (close together); 2, 10, 25, 40 has high variability (far apart)
vocabulary.cloze: How spread out the data values are is the ___.

conceptIntro.heading: What are mean, median, and mode?
conceptIntro.intro: Mean, median, and mode are three ways to find the center, or "typical" value, of a data set. The mean is the average, the median is the middle, and the mode is the most common value.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Mean = add then divide, median = the middle of the ordered numbers, mode = the value that shows up most.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My small data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9. There are 5 numbers.
Mean: add them, 2 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 9 = 25, then divide by 5. So the mean = 25 ÷ 5 = 5.
Median: the numbers are already in order. The middle (3rd) value is 4, so the median = 4.
Mode: the number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode = 4.

Next, what is the median? Which value is right in the middle?
Last, what is the mode? Which number appears the most times?

optional.stem: A player scored 4, 8, 6, 10, and 2 points across five quarters. What is the MEAN number of points?
optional.explanation: Add the points: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2 = 30. Divide by 5 quarters: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
choiceFeedback: Did you divide by something other than the number of quarters?
This is the sum—does the mean equal the sum?
The highest score is 10—is that the average of all the scores?
optional.stemEs: Un jugador anotó 4, 8, 6, 10 y 2 puntos en cinco cuartos. ¿Cuál es la MEDIA de puntos?
optional.explanationEs: Suma los puntos: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2 = 30. Divide entre 5 cuartos: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
hints: The mean is the amount each quarter would have if the points were shared out evenly.
Add all five scores together first, then divide by how many quarters there were.
Start the sum: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2. Once you have that total, divide it by 5.
hintsEs: La media es la cantidad que tendría cada cuarto si los puntos se repartieran por igual.
Suma primero los cinco puntajes y luego divide entre la cantidad de cuartos.
Empieza la suma: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2. Cuando tengas ese total, divídelo entre 5.

optional.stem: A goalie made 3, 7, 9, 2, and 5 saves in five games. What is the MEDIAN number of saves?
optional.explanation: Order the saves first: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle (3rd) value is 5, so the median is 5.
choiceFeedback: The highest value is 9—is median always the maximum?
List them in order first—then count to the middle.
The smallest value is 2—is the median always the smallest?
optional.stemEs: Un portero hizo 3, 7, 9, 2 y 5 atajadas en cinco partidos. ¿Cuál es la MEDIANA de atajadas?
optional.explanationEs: Ordena primero las atajadas: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. El valor del medio (el 3.º) es 5, así que la mediana es 5.
hints: The median is the value sitting in the middle once the data is in order.
Put the five save counts in order from least to greatest before you look for a middle.
In order they start 2, 3, ... — finish the ordering, then count in from both ends to find the value in the exact middle.
hintsEs: La mediana es el valor que queda en el medio una vez que los datos están ordenados.
Ordena las cinco cantidades de atajadas de menor a mayor antes de buscar el valor del medio.
Ordenadas empiezan así: 2, 3, ... Termina de ordenarlas y luego cuenta desde los dos extremos para hallar el valor que queda exactamente en el medio.

optional.stem: A team scored 4, 4, 7, and 9 goals in four matches. What is the MODE?
optional.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 4 shows up twice; every other value appears once. So the mode is 4.
choiceFeedback: 7 appears once—which number appears most often?
9 appears once—which number shows up more than once?
6 is the mean—is mean the same as mode?
optional.stemEs: Un equipo anotó 4, 4, 7 y 9 goles en cuatro partidos. ¿Cuál es la MODA?
optional.explanationEs: La moda es el valor que aparece con más frecuencia. El 4 aparece dos veces; los demás valores aparecen una vez. Así que la moda es 4.
hints: The mode is the value that shows up most often in a data set.
Count how many times each number appears instead of adding or averaging.
Go through 4, 4, 7, 9 and tally each value. The number with the largest tally is the mode.
hintsEs: La moda es el valor que aparece con más frecuencia en un conjunto de datos.
Cuenta cuántas veces aparece cada número en lugar de sumar o promediar.
Recorre 4, 4, 7, 9 y anota cuántas veces sale cada valor. El número con la mayor cuenta es la moda.

optional.label: Match each sports data set to the value of the measure named in CAPITALS.
optional.explanation: The capitalized word tells you which measure to compute: the game points 9, 3, 7, 5, 6 sum to 30 for a mean of 6, and the assists 14, 10, 18, 12, 16 sum to 70 for a mean of 14. The rebounds sort to 1, 3, 7, 8, 11 with a median of 7, and 9 appears three times in the jersey numbers, so its mode is 9.
optional.explanationEs: La palabra en mayúsculas te dice qué medida calcular: los puntos 9, 3, 7, 5, 6 suman 30 y dan una media de 6, y las asistencias 14, 10, 18, 12, 16 suman 70 y dan una media de 14. Los rebotes se ordenan como 1, 3, 7, 8, 11 con una mediana de 7, y el 9 aparece tres veces en los números de camiseta, así que su moda es 9.
hints: Each card names one measure in capital letters, so read that word first — the same data set would give a different answer for a different measure.
Mean means add and divide by the count, median means sort the list and take the middle, and mode means the value that repeats most.
Start with the rebounds card: reorder 8, 3, 11, 7, 1 from least to greatest, then look at the value sitting in the third position.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta nombra una medida en letras mayúsculas, así que lee esa palabra primero: el mismo conjunto de datos daría otra respuesta con otra medida.
Media significa sumar y dividir entre la cantidad, mediana significa ordenar la lista y tomar el centro, y moda significa el valor que más se repite.
Empieza con la tarjeta de rebotes: reordena 8, 3, 11, 7, 1 de menor a mayor y luego mira el valor que queda en la tercera posición.
optional.labelEs: Une cada conjunto de datos deportivos con el valor de la medida nombrada en MAYÚSCULAS.

optional.stem: One game was a 55-point outlier. Which measure of center best shows a TYPICAL game?
choices: The median, because the outlier barely moves the middle value
The mean, because it uses every score
The mode, because it is always the typical value
The range, because it shows the spread
optional.explanation: A high outlier pulls the mean upward, making it larger than most games. The median is the middle of the ordered data, so one unusual game barely changes it — it best describes a typical game.
choiceFeedback: The mean is pulled higher by the outlier—how does the median respond?
Mode is the most common value—does it handle outliers better than mean?
Range is 53—does range show a typical game?
optional.stemEs: Un partido fue un valor atípico de 55 puntos. ¿Cuál medida de centro muestra mejor un partido TÍPICO?
optional.explanationEs: Un valor atípico alto jala la media hacia arriba y la hace mayor que la mayoría de los partidos. La mediana es el centro de los datos ordenados, así que un partido inusual casi no la cambia: describe mejor un partido típico.
hints: An outlier is a value that sits far away from the rest of the data.
Think about which measure reacts to one huge number: the one built from a total, or the one built from position in the ordered list?
Picture replacing an ordinary score with 55. Recompute what happens to the total, then ask whether the middle value moved at all.
hintsEs: Un valor atípico es un valor que queda muy lejos del resto de los datos.
Piensa en cuál medida reacciona ante un número enorme: ¿la que se construye con una suma total o la que se construye con la posición en la lista ordenada?
Imagina que cambias un puntaje normal por 55. Vuelve a calcular qué le pasa al total y luego pregúntate si el valor del medio se movió.
choicesEs: La mediana, porque el valor atípico casi no mueve el valor del medio
La media, porque usa todos los puntajes
La moda, porque siempre es el valor típico
El rango, porque muestra la dispersión

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Median Mistake

workedExample.label: Goal
workedExample.work: Find the median number of points.

workedExample.label: Pick the middle
workedExample.work: The number in the middle of the list is 7, so the median = 7.

optional.correctWork: You must ORDER the data before finding the middle. Ordered least to greatest: 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. The true middle (3rd) value is 6, so the median = 6, not 7.
hints: The median is the middle of the data ONLY after it is sorted from least to greatest.
Reorder 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 → 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. Now find the middle value.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — El error de la mediana
optional.explanation: The 7 sits in the middle of the list as written, but the list was never sorted. Ordered least to greatest the data is 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, so the true third value — and the median — is 6.
optional.explanationEs: El 7 está en el centro de la lista tal como está escrita, pero la lista nunca se ordenó. Ordenada de menor a mayor, los datos son 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, así que el verdadero tercer valor —y la mediana— es 6.

choiceFeedback: Add the numbers first—does 14 equal the sum divided by 5?
Did you forget to divide by the count of numbers?
Is 60 the mean, or the sum?
hints: Mean means the average of all five numbers — you'll need both a total and how many numbers there are.
Use the formula: mean = sum of the values ÷ how many values. Count first: there are 5 numbers here.
Step 1: add 10 + 14 + 8 + 12 + 16 to get the total. Then divide that total by 5 — the result is the mean.
hintsEs: La media es el promedio de los cinco números: necesitarás tanto un total como cuántos números hay.
Usa la fórmula: media = suma de los valores ÷ cuántos valores hay. Cuenta primero: aquí hay 5 números.
Paso 1: suma 10 + 14 + 8 + 12 + 16 para obtener el total. Luego divide ese total entre 5: el resultado es la media.

choiceFeedback: Did you order them first? What's the middle value after ordering?
The lowest is 3—is median always the lowest?
7 is not the middle value—order them first.
hints: Median = the middle number, but only AFTER the list is in order. Don't pick the middle of the unsorted list.
Rewrite 3, 7, 2, 9, 5 from least to greatest, then count in from both ends until you reach the one value in the exact middle.
Start ordering: the smallest is 2, then 3... finish the ordered list of all five values, then circle the 3rd one — that's the median.
approaching.explanationEs: Ordenados: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. El valor del medio es 5.
hintsEs: La mediana es el número del medio, pero solo DESPUÉS de ordenar la lista. No elijas el del medio de la lista sin ordenar.
Reescribe 3, 7, 2, 9, 5 de menor a mayor y luego cuenta desde ambos extremos hasta llegar al único valor que queda justo en el medio.
Empieza a ordenar: el menor es 2, luego 3… termina la lista ordenada de los cinco valores y luego encierra el 3.º: esa es la mediana.

approaching.explanation: 4 appears three times — more than any other value. Mode = 4.
choiceFeedback: 7 appears once—which number appears most often?
9 appears once—count how many times each number shows up.
2 appears once—is mode the smallest or most frequent?
hints: Mode is about repeats — which value shows up in the list more times than any other?
Make a quick tally: write each different number and count how many times it appears in 4, 7, 4, 9, 2, 4, 8.
Start your tally: 7 appears once, 9 appears once... keep counting every number and pick the one with the highest tally.
approaching.explanationEs: El 4 aparece tres veces, más que cualquier otro valor. Moda = 4.
hintsEs: La moda tiene que ver con repeticiones: ¿qué valor aparece en la lista más veces que cualquier otro?
Haz un conteo rápido: escribe cada número distinto y cuenta cuántas veces aparece en 4, 7, 4, 9, 2, 4, 8.
Empieza tu conteo: el 7 aparece una vez, el 9 aparece una vez… sigue contando cada número y elige el de mayor conteo.

choiceFeedback: Add them up first, then divide by 5—not just multiply.
Count the numbers (5)—divide the sum by 5.
This is the sum—is sum the same as mean?
hints: Watch out: one tempting answer is just the total of the list. The mean asks you to go one step further.
Mean = total ÷ count. There are 5 values in this list, so after adding you must divide by 5.
Step 1: add 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14. Step 2: take that total and divide it by 5. The quotient is your mean.
hintsEs: Cuidado: una respuesta tentadora es solo el total de la lista. La media te pide dar un paso más.
Media = total ÷ cantidad. Hay 5 valores en esta lista, así que después de sumar debes dividir entre 5.
Paso 1: suma 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14. Paso 2: toma ese total y divídelo entre 5. El cociente es tu media.

approaching.instructions: Sort each step into the correct order for finding the median.

categories.label: Steps to find the median (in order)
items: Step 1: Order the data from least to greatest
Step 2: Count the total number of values
Step 3: Find the middle value (or average of two middle values)
Step 4: The middle value is the median

hints: You must order the data FIRST before finding the middle.
If there is an even number of values, average the two middle values.
approaching.label: Put the steps for finding median in the correct order.
approaching.explanation: Ordering the data comes first, because the middle of an unsorted list is not the median. After ordering, counting the values tells you whether there is one middle number or two to average, and only then does the middle value become the median.
approaching.explanationEs: Ordenar los datos va primero, porque el centro de una lista sin ordenar no es la mediana. Después de ordenar, contar los valores te dice si hay un solo número central o dos que hay que promediar, y solo entonces el valor del centro se convierte en la mediana.
approaching.labelEs: Pon en orden correcto los pasos para encontrar la mediana.
hintsEs: Debes ordenar los datos PRIMERO antes de hallar el valor del medio.
Si hay una cantidad par de valores, promedia los dos valores del medio.

approaching.title: The Mean Mistake (forgot to divide)

workedExample.label: Data set
workedExample.work: A player scored 6, 8, 10, and 6 points in 4 games.

workedExample.label: Goal
workedExample.work: Find the MEAN number of points.

approaching.correctWork: Adding is only half of the mean. After adding (sum = 30) you must DIVIDE by how many values there are: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5. The mean is 7.5 points, not 30.
hints: Mean = add then DIVIDE. The total of 30 is just the sum, not the mean.
There are 4 values, so divide the sum by 4: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5.
approaching.titleEs: El error de la media (olvidó dividir)
approaching.explanation: The sum 6 + 8 + 10 + 6 = 30 is correct, but the answer stops there. The mean shares the total evenly across all the games, so you divide by the 4 values: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 points. A mean of 30 is also impossible here, since no single game reached 30 points.
approaching.explanationEs: La suma 6 + 8 + 10 + 6 = 30 está bien, pero la respuesta se detiene ahí. La media reparte el total en partes iguales entre todos los juegos, así que se divide entre los 4 valores: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 puntos. Una media de 30 también sería imposible aquí, porque ningún juego llegó a 30 puntos.

hints: Each row needs three different measures: mean (average), median (middle of the ordered list), and mode (most frequent value).
Do one row at a time: add and divide by the count for mean; reorder the list for median; tally repeats for mode. Round means to 2 decimals.
Row 1 (5, 8, 8, 10, 14): add the five values and divide by 5 for the mean. The list is already ordered, so the median is the 3rd value.
onLevel.explanation: Row 1 (5, 8, 8, 10, 14) has a sum of 45, so the mean is 45 ÷ 5 = 9, the third value 8 is the median, and 8 repeats so it is the mode. Row 2 gives 160 ÷ 6 ≈ 26.67 with median and mode both 25, and Row 3 gives 610 ÷ 6 ≈ 101.67 with the two middle values 100 and 100 averaging to a median of 100, which is also the mode.
onLevel.explanationEs: La fila 1 (5, 8, 8, 10, 14) suma 45, así que la media es 45 ÷ 5 = 9, el tercer valor 8 es la mediana, y 8 se repite, así que es la moda. La fila 2 da 160 ÷ 6 ≈ 26.67 con mediana y moda de 25, y la fila 3 da 610 ÷ 6 ≈ 101.67 con los dos valores centrales 100 y 100 que promedian una mediana de 100, que también es la moda.
hintsEs: Cada fila necesita tres medidas distintas: media (promedio), mediana (el medio de la lista ordenada) y moda (el valor más frecuente).
Haz una fila a la vez: suma y divide entre la cantidad para la media; reordena la lista para la mediana; cuenta repeticiones para la moda. Redondea las medias a 2 decimales.
Fila 1 (5, 8, 8, 10, 14): suma los cinco valores y divide entre 5 para la media. La lista ya está ordenada, así que la mediana es el 3.º valor.

onLevel.label: Match each measure to its definition.
hints: These are the four core vocabulary words of this unit — each pairs with a short formula or phrase that defines it.
Use word clues: 'mean' is the average (uses ÷), 'median' sounds like 'middle', 'mode' starts like 'most', 'range' is how far the data reaches.
Start with Median: 'med-' is like 'middle' — pair it with the middle-value card, then match the remaining three by their clues.
onLevel.explanation: Each term pairs with what you actually do to the data: mean is sum ÷ count, median is the middle value of the ordered list, mode is the most frequent value, and range is max − min. Mean and range are computed from arithmetic, while median and mode come from the position and repetition of values.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada término se une con lo que realmente le haces a los datos: la media es suma ÷ cantidad, la mediana es el valor del centro de la lista ordenada, la moda es el valor más frecuente, y el rango es máximo − mínimo. La media y el rango se calculan con operaciones, mientras que la mediana y la moda salen de la posición y la repetición de los valores.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada medida con su definición.
hintsEs: Estas son las cuatro palabras clave de la unidad; cada una va con una fórmula corta o una frase que la define.
Usa las pistas de las palabras: 'media' es el promedio (usa ÷), 'mediana' suena a 'medio', 'moda' es lo que 'más' se repite, y 'rango' es cuánto se extienden los datos.
Empieza con Mediana: 'medi-' es como 'medio'; únela con la tarjeta del valor central y luego empareja las otras tres por sus pistas.

onLevel.label: Data: 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. Place the mean and median on the number line.
hints: Ordered data: 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. Middle value = 30. When data is symmetric, mean = median.
onLevel.explanation: The five values add to 150, so the mean is 150 ÷ 5 = 30, and the ordered list 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 puts 30 in the middle as well. Both markers land on the same tick because this data is spaced evenly around its center, so no value pulls the mean away from the middle.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los cinco valores suman 150, así que la media es 150 ÷ 5 = 30, y la lista ordenada 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 también deja 30 en el centro. Las dos marcas caen en la misma marca porque estos datos están repartidos de manera pareja alrededor de su centro, así que ningún valor jala la media lejos del medio.

onLevel.stem: Data set: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. What is the median?
onLevel.explanation: With 6 values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
choiceFeedback: With an even count, take the average of the two middle values.
The two middle values are 6 and 8—what's their average?
Don't add all values and divide—find the middle two values.
hints: Count the values: there are 6, an even number — so no single value sits exactly in the middle.
With an even count, the median is the average of the TWO middle values. In an ordered list of 6, those are the 3rd and 4th.
The list is already ordered. Step 1: circle the 3rd and 4th values. Step 2: add them and divide by 2 — that result is the median.
onLevel.stemEs: Conjunto de datos: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. ¿Cuál es la mediana?
onLevel.explanationEs: Con 6 valores, la mediana es el promedio del 3.º y el 4.º valor: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores: hay 6, un número par, así que ningún valor queda exactamente en el medio.
Con una cantidad par, la mediana es el promedio de los DOS valores centrales. En una lista ordenada de 6, esos son el 3.º y el 4.º.
La lista ya está ordenada. Paso 1: encierra el 3.º y el 4.º valor. Paso 2: súmalos y divide entre 2; ese resultado es la mediana.

onLevel.title: The Even-Count Median Mistake

workedExample.label: Data set
workedExample.work: Points per game, in order: 3, 8, 10, 14, 16, 20 (6 values)

workedExample.label: Goal
workedExample.work: Find the MEDIAN number of points.

workedExample.label: Pick the middle
workedExample.work: With 6 values the student grabs a single middle number and says median = 10.

onLevel.correctWork: When a data set has an EVEN number of values there is no single middle number. You must average the TWO middle values. Here the 3rd and 4th values are 10 and 14, so the median = (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, not 10.
hints: With an even number of values, there are two numbers in the middle — average them.
The two middle values are 10 and 14: (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12.
onLevel.titleEs: El error de la mediana con cantidad par
onLevel.explanation: With 6 values there is no single number sitting in the middle — positions 3 and 4 tie for the center. The 3rd and 4th values are 10 and 14, so the median is their average, (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, not just the lower one.
onLevel.explanationEs: Con 6 valores no hay un solo número en el centro: las posiciones 3 y 4 empatan en el medio. El 3.º y el 4.º valor son 10 y 14, así que la mediana es su promedio, (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, y no solo el menor de los dos.

extending.title: Find the Stats Error
extending.correctWork: Mode = 15 (appears twice, more than any other value). Mode is the most frequent value, not the largest.
hints: Mode means 'most often,' not 'most.' Which number appears the most times?
15 appears twice. No other number repeats. So the mode is 15, not 18.
extending.explanation: The mean and median steps are both correct; the mode step picks 18 because it is the biggest number. Mode means most often, not most, and in 12, 15, 15, 18, 20 only 15 repeats, so the mode is 15.
extending.explanationEs: Los pasos de la media y la mediana están correctos; el paso de la moda elige 18 porque es el número más grande. Moda significa el más frecuente, no el mayor, y en 12, 15, 15, 18, 20 solo 15 se repite, así que la moda es 15.

extending.prompt: A basketball player scored 15, 18, 16, 42, and 14 points in 5 games. Find the mean and median. Which better represents the player's typical game? Explain how the outlier affects each measure.
extending.sentenceFrame: Mean = ___. Median = ___. The ___ better represents a typical game because the outlier (___) pulls the ___ toward it, making it ___ than most scores. The median is not affected because ___.
extending.hint: Start by adding all the scores, then divide by how many games were played.
hints: One game (42 points) is far above the others — that's your outlier. Keep it in mind as you find both measures.
Plan: (1) mean = sum of the 5 scores ÷ 5, (2) median = middle of the ordered scores, (3) decide which lands closer to most games.
Step 1: add 15 + 18 + 16 + 42 + 14 and divide by 5. Then order the scores least to greatest and circle the 3rd — compare the two results.
extending.explanation: The five scores add to 105, so the mean is 105 ÷ 5 = 21, while the ordered list 14, 15, 16, 18, 42 gives a median of 16. The 42-point game is an outlier that drags the mean up above four of the five games, but the median only cares about position, so 16 better represents a typical game.
extending.explanationEs: Los cinco puntajes suman 105, así que la media es 105 ÷ 5 = 21, mientras que la lista ordenada 14, 15, 16, 18, 42 da una mediana de 16. El juego de 42 puntos es un valor atípico que jala la media por encima de cuatro de los cinco juegos, pero a la mediana solo le importa la posición, así que 16 representa mejor un juego típico.
extending.promptEs: Un jugador de baloncesto anotó 15, 18, 16, 42 y 14 puntos en 5 partidos. Encuentra la media y la mediana. ¿Cuál representa mejor un partido típico del jugador? Explica cómo afecta el valor atípico a cada medida.
hintsEs: Un partido (42 puntos) está muy por encima de los demás: ese es tu valor atípico. Tenlo presente al hallar ambas medidas.
Plan: (1) media = suma de los 5 puntajes ÷ 5, (2) mediana = el medio de los puntajes ordenados, (3) decide cuál queda más cerca de la mayoría de los partidos.
Paso 1: suma 15 + 18 + 16 + 42 + 14 y divide entre 5. Luego ordena los puntajes de menor a mayor, encierra el 3.º y compara los dos resultados.

editableCells.answer: Both work — no outlier, data is symmetric
Median — the outlier 50 pulls the mean to 19.2, which is higher than 4 of the 5 values

hints: The two rows are almost identical — only the last value changes from 12 to 50. Watch what that single change does to each measure.
For each row: mean = sum ÷ 5; median = middle of the ordered list. Compare the two measures within each row before choosing which is better.
Row 1 first: add 10 + 12 + 11 + 13 + 12, divide by 5, and order the list to find the middle. Save Row 2 to see how the 50 shifts things.
extending.explanation: Row 1 sums to 58, so its mean is 11.6 and its ordered middle is 12 — the two measures nearly agree because no value is far from the rest. Changing only the last value to 50 pushes the sum to 96 and the mean to 19.2, above four of the five values, while the median stays 12, which is why the median is the better description for Row 2.
extending.explanationEs: La fila 1 suma 58, así que su media es 11.6 y su centro ordenado es 12: las dos medidas casi coinciden porque ningún valor está lejos de los demás. Cambiar solo el último valor a 50 sube la suma a 96 y la media a 19.2, por encima de cuatro de los cinco valores, mientras que la mediana sigue siendo 12, y por eso la mediana describe mejor la fila 2.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Mean, Median, and Mode is finding the median without ordering the data first — students pick the middle number straight from the list as given (for 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 they say the median is 7, the middle position in that original order) instead of sorting least to greatest (2, 4, 6, 7, 9) and finding the true middle value, 6. Before finalizing a median, always reorder the data smallest to largest, then count to the middle position — and if there is an even number of values, average the two middle numbers.

diagram.title: Class Quiz Scores — Dot Plot
diagram.caption: The tallest stack sits at 92 — the mode. The balance point (mean) is 86.6. Both describe the center, but they land in different places.

connect.scenario: Your class took a math quiz. The scores were: 85, 92, 78, 88, 92, 95, 72, 88, 92, 84. The teacher says 'most students scored around 87.' A student disagrees and says 'the most common score was 92.'
connect.promptQuestion: Who is using the mean, and who is using the mode? Which is more useful here?
connect.prompt: The teacher used the ___ (about 86.6). The student used the ___ (92). The ___ is more useful here because ___.

check.stem: The teacher said 'most students scored around 87.' Which measure is that?
choices: The mean (average)
The mode
The median
The range
check.explanation: The mean is the balance point: 866 ÷ 10 = 86.6, which rounds to about 87.

check.stem: The student said 'the most common score was 92.' Which measure is that?
choices: The mode
The mean
The median
The range
check.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 92 shows up three times — more than any other score.

check.stem: What is the median of the 10 scores?
check.explanation: In order: 72, 78, 84, 85, 88, 88, 92, 92, 92, 95. With 10 values the median is the average of the 5th and 6th: (88 + 88) ÷ 2 = 88.

connect.modelAnswer: The teacher used the MEAN: 866 ÷ 10 = 86.6, about 87. The student used the MODE: 92 appears three times, more than any other score. Both are correct measures of center — they simply answer different questions. The mean is the balance point of all the scores; the mode is the single most common score.

exitTicket.stem: Data set: 4, 7, 10, 7, 12. What is the median?
choiceFeedback: Order the values first, then find the exact middle one.
The median is the middle of the ORDERED list, not the largest.
Sort the numbers and pick the center — 4 is the smallest.
hints: Median means middle — but the list 4, 7, 10, 7, 12 isn't in order yet. That's your first job.
Rewrite the five values from least to greatest, then count in one value at a time from each end until you meet in the middle.
Start the ordered list: 4 is the smallest value. Keep placing values least to greatest, then circle the 3rd of the 5 — that position is the median.

questions.stem: Which question is NOT a statistical question?
choices: How many home runs did each player hit this year?
How many innings are in a baseball game?
How many miles does each runner train per week?
How tall is each player on the basketball team?
questions.explanation: "How many innings are in a baseball game?" has one fixed answer (9) — no variability. The other questions all produce different answers for different people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a statistical question?
choices: How many points are scored for a free throw?
How many points did each player score this season?
What sport does this team play?
How many halves are in a soccer game?
questions.explanation: "How many points did each player score?" is statistical because different players will have different scores — there is variability in the data.

questions.stem: Why is 'How many hours of sleep did each student get last night?' a statistical question?
choices: Because it asks about sleep
Because hours are numbers
Because the answer is always 8 hours
Because different students got different amounts of sleep
questions.explanation: A statistical question anticipates variability — different students slept different amounts, so the data will vary.
